title: Handling a page fault
purpose: Explain the ordered valid nonresident-page fault handling path, including rejecting illegal accesses.
requiredChecks: Six numbered steps appear in correct order: reference, trap, validate/locate, acquire frame/load, update page table, restart.
Illegal address terminates/raises an error; only a valid nonresident page proceeds to disk load.
Backing storage supplies the missing page to a free frame, and present bit becomes1 before restart.
Restart is the interrupted instruction, not a new process; every label is complete and arrows follow the stated order.
alt: Page fault handling: trap, validate the address, load a valid missing page, update the page table, and restart the interrupted instruction
prompt:
Create a NEW original technical educational diagram for an English operating-systems blog. White background, dark navy crisp sans-serif text, blue and teal flat boxes, clean thin arrows, ample whitespace, large legible labels, no copied textbook artwork, no logos or watermark. TITLE "Handling a page fault". Make a readable landscape FLOWCHART with exactly six numbered main boxes, alternating across TWO rows with clear connecting arrows in ascending numeric order. Use these exact texts, line breaks as needed:
"1  Reference a nonresident page"
"2  Trap to the operating system"
"3  Validate address and locate page"
"4  Acquire a free frame and load page"
"5  Update page table: Present = 1"
"6  Restart the interrupted instruction".
Under step3 add a short branch labeled "Illegal address" leading to a separate red-outline box "Terminate / report error". The main step3→4 arrow is labeled "Valid address". Near step4 put simple small supporting boxes "Backing storage" and "Physical memory — free frame" with a one-way arrow labeled "Read missing page" from Backing storage to the free frame. Step5 must come AFTER this disk read. Do not draw a loop that restarts before the table is updated. At final step label the restart as the interrupted instruction (not a fresh process). Keep arrows and branch topology simple and unambiguous. Exact spelling mandatory; no more than these six numbered steps.
